1001.author: ink999107
1001.body:
A managed shell execution could stay `running` forever even though its command had already finished. `runSandboxed` waited only for the child process's `close` event, and Node emits `close` only after every writer of the inherited stdio pipes is gone. A descendant the command left behind — a background process, a fork, the egress bridge's child — keeps those pipes open, so `close` never arrives.

Managed executions are forced to `executionTimeoutMs = 0`, so the only other settle path (the timeout branch) never existed for them. Executions are serial per workspace root, so the stuck head kept every later execution `queued`, and `cancel` only sent SIGKILL without any join deadline: the API answered 200/202 while the record stayed `running`. In the report that prompted this change, a real E2E burned its whole one-hour budget on a command whose logs were already complete.

## Settle on `exit`, not only on `close`

`runSandboxed` now also listens for `exit`. Once the commanded process has exited, a bounded grace period (`DEFAULT_TERMINATION_GRACE_MS`, 10 s) starts for `close`; if `close` is still missing (a descendant holds the pipes), the exit itself is the outcome. Output already read is kept, and a paused stream is drained the same way the timeout branch does. `finish` clears both timers, and `stopError` (abort, quota, timeout) still wins over a signalled exit, preserving the existing semantics. A command that keeps running without a deadline is unaffected.

## Bound the join after a kill

SIGKILL is asynchronous, and a process in uninterruptible I/O — or a group that vanished — may never report `exit`. Every `stop()` now starts a join deadline. If the process has exited by then, it settles normally; if not, the run rejects with `ProcessTerminationUnverifiedError` (`code: PROCESS_TERMINATION_UNVERIFIED`). The `ExecutionManager` records that as `unknown` and quarantines the workspace through the existing mechanism, instead of fabricating `processTerminated: true` or committing a snapshot while a writer may still exist. Because the queue item resolves, the Workspace queue advances; work already queued behind the quarantine is rejected at dispatch with `EXECUTION_RESOURCE_QUARANTINED` rather than launched into unverified state.

## Cancel a queued execution immediately

`cancel()` used to abort a controller that the queued work would only observe after the head finished, so a cancelled `queued` execution looked unchanged indefinitely. A `queued` record now becomes `cancelled` (`not_started` evidence, `finishedAt`) and is aborted in the same call. The tail still waits on the head — one workspace stays serial — and the cancelled command is skipped at dispatch. A re-check after recovery validation closes the window where a cancellation arriving during that `await` could still launch a process, and a record that never launched is no longer briefly written back as `running`.

## Respect an operator-configured lifetime

`POST /shell-executions` used to overwrite `executionTimeoutMs` with 0 unconditionally. The client's waiting deadline is still not the process lifetime, but an operator who set `SCIENCE_AGENT_EXEC_TIMEOUT_MS` now actually gets that lifetime bound for managed executions. The default remains unlimited.

## Validation

Run on this commit (`be90a20e`) with the repository's three layers.

- UT: planned 6905, executed 6876, passed 6861, failed 15, skipped 0. `services/runner` passes in full, including the three new cases (a managed execution settles when `close` is missed; a kill whose exit is never observed settles as unverified; a queued cancel is terminal without starting the next one). Every one of the 15 failures reproduces on unmodified `main` in this environment, so none is introduced here:
  - `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` (5) and `services/launcher/src/source-evolve.test.ts` (5): the stack they spawn exits with status 1 before its health gate.
  - `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`, `services/api/src/evolution/evolve-thinking-entry.test.ts`: the same cases fail on `main`.
  - `services/api/src/server.test.ts`: a different single case fails in each run, which is flakiness rather than a fixed regression.
  - `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`: the host's bubblewrap 0.6.1 has no `--disable-userns`, which the case hard-codes.
  - `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`: JiuwenSwarm cannot be installed here (the pinned `openai-codex` is absent from the local mirror); the same case fails on `main`.
- ST: planned 51, executed 51, passed 50, failed 1 — `test/api/evolve-distribution.test.ts` cannot download the pinned CPython build from the GitHub release (HTTP 504 on this network); the unmodified `main` run fails there too. `check:swarm-sdk-contract` passed against an existing JiuwenSwarm install (79 tests and 20 subtests).
- E2E: planned 136 mocked browser cases. See the next section.

## E2E user journeys

PASS for the batches that completed on `be90a20e` on this host, with the failures below attributed. Mocked browser layer against the real local stack (bubblewrap, JiuwenSwarm backend, pinned Chromium), six serial batches from the frozen 136-case plan:

- `mocked-governed` 5 passed / 0 failed, `mocked-literature` 6 / 0, `mocked-research` 21 / 0, `mocked-standard-config-fresh` 2 / 0.
- `mocked-standard-config-global` 37 passed / 3 failed. `journey-prepare-environment` was BLOCKED with `micromamba setup failed` (this host has no micromamba base Python for the managed environment). `journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings` missed its 10 s success-alert wait once and passed when the same spec was rerun against the same stack, so it is load-sensitive rather than a fixed regression. `journey-model-connect-wizard` fails its first layout assertion on this host: the submit button's bottom edge measures 598.2 px against a dialog footer fixed at 580 px. This commit changes only `services/runner` — no web code — so that measurement belongs to the host's renderer, not to this change.
- `mocked-standard-journeys` 56 passed / 0 failed before the local per-invocation cap stopped the batch with 6 of its 62 cases still queued behind the long sandbox-network and session journeys.

Totals executed: 130 of 136 — 127 passed, 3 failed, 0 skipped. The three failures are the environment BLOCKED case, the load-sensitive spec that passed on rerun, and the host layout assertion. GitHub Actions runs the full matrix with its own budget.

## Release

Release category: `release:fix` (the GitHub label is pending a maintainer; this account has no write access to the upstream repository)

User impact: a session no longer wedges when a command leaves a background process holding its pipes; Stop/cancel always reaches a terminal state, and the executions queued behind it run instead of waiting forever.

Compatibility and migration: none. The default lifetime stays unlimited; the new grace period only applies after the commanded process has exited or a kill was requested.
1001.head: fix/runner-execution-wedge
1001.title: fix(runner): settle an execution whose process ended but close was missed

1002.author: yuanzhou75
1002.body:
Fixes #997

## The defect

The agent could create, read and price an evolution search but not stop one. When the user corrected the scoring formula mid-run, the only move the tool surface allowed was to start a second search beside the first — the issue's evidence shows two concurrent PUCT runs on one session (`c870cf09` candidates=12, `fee68bb2` candidates=1, both `running`), each frozen against a different formula and splitting the same budget, with no way for the user to say which result counts.

The server could already stop a run (`POST /api/evolve/runs/{id}/stop`, which the desktop uses); only the agent-facing capability was missing.

## Change

- **`packages/evolve`**: `EvolveToolRuntime` gains an optional `stopEvolveRun`, and `createEvolveTools` registers `stop_evolve_run` only when the deployment can actually stop a run — the same shape `createIdeaResearch` already uses, so a deployment without the capability does not advertise a tool that pretends to work.
- The tool takes an explicit `runId` and no "most recent" default, because stopping is destructive. It answers with what actually happened: `stopping` for an active run, and the terminal status when the search had already finished (that case is not an error).
- **`services/api/src/bootstrap/platform.ts`** implements it on the same orchestrator call the desktop route uses, scoped to the asking session: an id from another session is refused, and an unknown id answers with the searches this session does have — the same help `get_evolve_run` gives, since the reader is a model deciding what to call next.
- The description carries the rule the issue is about: stop the running search **before** proposing a replacement, and never start a second search alongside a live one.
- Docs list the tool in both languages.

## Tests

`packages/evolve/src/index.test.ts`:
- the stop tool is absent without the capability and present with it;
- the run id is passed through unchanged and the reply names the run;
- an already-finished search is reported as such rather than as a stop.

CI covers the composition root: `native-agent.test.ts` builds a runtime without `stopEvolveRun` (the optional member keeps that fixture valid), and the `services/api` build exercises the new implementation.

## Scope

This is the agent-side capability the issue asks for. It does not add server-side rejection of a second concurrent run on the same session — the issue phrases that as "and/or", and the stop tool makes the correct sequence available. If the reviewers want the guard as well, that is a separate change and the issue can carry it.
1002.head: fix-997-stop-evolve-run
1002.title: fix(evolve): give the agent a stop_evolve_run tool

1003.author: ink999107
1003.body:
The web front end is being replaced by the desktop entry, but the merged live literature review case still drove the old web page: it created its fixture through `createProjectAndSession`, opened the Session with `openProjectSession`, and submitted the question with `sendUserMessage`. This change moves the case to the desktop entry, so the journey keeps covering the surface a reader actually uses, without changing what it verifies about the literature work.

## The case now drives the desktop entry

`test/literature-review-immune-liver-real.spec.ts` becomes `test/desktop-literature-review-immune-liver-real.spec.ts`. It starts the Vite entry on 4178 (`startDesktopEntry`), seeds the shared token into the origin's localStorage before the first navigation (`seedDesktopOrigin` — the desktop app reads it from there rather than from the shared storage state), creates the fixture with `createDesktopFixture`, opens the Session with `openDesktopSession`, and submits the fixed question from `#composer-textarea` with `sendMessage`.

The stack health gate now probes the same origin the helper drives (`API_ORIGIN`). Previously the probe could pass against one port and the journey then drive another.

Everything the case verifies is unchanged and still read from the control API: the five literature MCP sources are installed and ready, only those connectors are enabled, every skill and specialist is off, PubMed and bioRxiv are each invoked successfully, the declared CSV has exactly 14 unique pathways with integer counts on both sides, the chart is a real PNG or SVG naming both populations, and the review has Methods / Results / Contradictory findings / References, names both databases, and cites at least four distinct papers. Only the entry point and the surfaces the reader acts on moved.

## The desktop fixture takes the shared catalog's model policy

`createDesktopFixture(page)` used to create an owned model from `E2E_LLM_VARIANT` (defaulting to `openai`) and start a Session with no thinking policy. That was enough for the evolve smoke, but the shared real catalog names the variant `E2E_LLM_API_VARIANT`, and the web journeys also set a thinking policy. `resolveModel` now reads `E2E_LLM_API_VARIANT` first and falls back to the old spelling, and `createDesktopFixture` accepts `{ name, model, session }`:

- `name` — the base name for the Project, the Session and an owned model profile;
- `modelId` — the id of a profile already on the stack; when set no profile is created and `model` is ignored. The helper's reuse path also accepts `E2E_LLM_MODEL_ID`, the shared catalog's spelling of `E2E_MODEL_ID`, so a stack that registers its model ahead of the run works without the `E2E_LLM_BASE_URL` credentials;
- `model` — extra profile fields such as `apiVariant`, `thinkingMode` and `thinkingEffort`. The profile is spread first in the create body, so it cannot replace the endpoint, the token or the name; `apiVariant` is taken from it when present and from the environment otherwise;
- `session` — fields set on the Session together with its model, kept in the same request because a mode switch must stay in its own request.

The defaults reproduce the previous behaviour exactly (`Desktop SRBench <suffix>`, `E2E_LLM_VARIANT`, no Session fields), so the evolve smoke is unaffected.

## Validation

The branch is rebased onto `upstream/main` at `95d5bdb5`; upstream has since advanced to `239dde7d`, and none of the new commits touch either changed file. The diff is +90/−45 over 2 files.

The review follow-up `f7865449` (reuse a pre-registered model) changes only the helper's reuse path and the fixture call; on it `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes and `pnpm ci:l1` passes 4/4. The runs below were measured on `373c6137`, which exercises the create path and the journey the follow-up does not alter.

Run locally on `373c6137` (Linux x64):

| Layer | Planned | Executed | Passed | Failed | Skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UT | 6900 | 6900 | 6885 | 15 | 0 |
| E2E (mocked) | 136 | 136 | 133 | 3 | 0 |

The 15 UT failures are host limitations, none in this diff:

- **10 — `services/launcher/src/serve.test.ts` and `source-evolve.test.ts`.** They write CommonJS fixtures under `os.tmpdir()`; this host carries an unrelated `/tmp/package.json` with `"type": "module"`, so Node parses the fixture as ESM. Re-running the same tests with `TMPDIR=/var/tmp/...` passes. The same set was reproduced on a pristine `upstream/main` worktree when PR #964 recorded its baseline.
- **1 — `scripts/start-stack-lock.test.mjs`, "the same harness FAILS on the pre-fix body that restored only on the happy path".** The same failure is present on pristine `upstream/main` on this host.
- **1 — `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.test.ts`, the trajectory assertion.** The same failure is present on earlier branches of this work on this host.
- **1 — `services/runner/src/sandbox-network.test.ts`.** The host's `bwrap` has no `--disable-userns`.
- **1 — `scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`.** A worker-level failure under the full run; the file passes 1/1 when run alone (`node --test scripts/race-contract.test.mjs`).
- **1 — `check:research-python-ut`.** `uv` cannot reach `pypi.org` from this host (`operation timed out` fetching `charset-normalizer`).

The mocked E2E layer ran 136 planned / 136 executed / 133 passed / 3 failed / 0 skipped. Two are the failures PR #964 already recorded on this host: `journey-model-connect-wizard` measures the connect card at 598.2 px against a `< 580` bound (a web layout measurement, `apps/web` untouched here), and `journey-prepare-environment` J3 is `BLOCKED: managed Python base is not ready (failed: micromamba setup failed)` because the pinned micromamba release is on `github.com`, which this host cannot reach. The third, `journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings`, is a full-suite flake: it timed out after 10 s waiting for the success alert its own stub produces, and both of its journeys pass 2/2 when the spec runs alone on the same commit (`CI_E2E_SPEC=test/journey-custom-provider-degraded-settings.spec.ts .ci/run-e2e.sh mocked`).

## E2E user journeys

Real stack, live model, on `373c6137` — PASS. The full run took 1119.1 s (18.7 min) with 3 of 3 journey steps passing:

| Step | Expected | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turn skills, specialists and the Reviewer off, enable every literature MCP source | no skill whitelist, no specialist, automatic review off, only the literature connectors enabled, PubMed and bioRxiv ready | PASS |
| Ask the fixed liver immune-pathway question from the desktop composer and wait for the main Run chain | the desktop entry opens the Session, the model runs the prompt with literature-only MCP tools, the main Run chain reaches a terminal state | PASS |
| Verify live PubMed and bioRxiv searches and the 14-pathway delivery | PubMed returned records, bioRxiv ran successfully, 14 unique pathways with integer counts on both sides, a real PNG/SVG chart, and a review with all four sections citing at least four distinct papers | PASS |

The delivered evidence from that run: PubMed invoked 9 times returning 79 records; bioRxiv invoked 3 times returning 0 preprints in its trailing window (the review states this rather than inventing one); 14 CSV rows with 9 adult and 11 pediatric nonzero counts; the chart is a 36,964-byte PNG; 15 citations (8 PMIDs, 7 DOIs) across the review, with a Contradictory findings section present; final delivery status `passed` with no delivery errors. The runner ledger for the run shows 19 shell executions, all terminal (15 completed, 4 failed) — no execution left `running` or `queued`.

## Release

Release category: release:internal

The GitHub label is pending a maintainer: this account is an outside contributor and cannot apply labels to the upstream repository.

User impact: none — this is the repository's real E2E journey and its desktop fixture helper.

Compatibility and migration: none. Existing callers of `createDesktopFixture(page)` keep the previous defaults.

1003.title: test(e2e): drive the literature review case through the desktop entry

1004.author: yuanzhou75
1004.body:
Fixes #998 (`Refs #978`)

## The gap

#987 settles one half of #978: `!execution.accepted && submissionRejected` → `rejectSubmission`, so a Runner that refuses the submission makes the tool call fail visibly.

The 4th #978 reproduction is the other half — `accepted=true stage=finalization`, where the Runner answers 401 `Execution not found for this Agent` while the finished execution's result is being handed over. That error does not match the submission branch, so it fell through to `unavailable()` → `state="unknown"`, `finalization="pending"`, `retryable=false`. No terminal state, no tool result, and the run stays `running` until the idle watchdog — the same missing invariant as #978, reached through a different stage.

## Change

- An accepted execution that the Runner answers with **401/403/404** is settled **failed with committed provenance**. Those answers mean "this execution is not readable by this Agent any more", which no amount of waiting changes, so leaving the record unknown only keeps the tool call and the run alive.
- The message states what is actually known rather than implying the command never ran: the Runner accepted the command, may have run it, would not return the result, and the workspace should be inspected before anything is re-run.
- The submission-stage path (#987) and the `PROCESS_STATE_UNVERIFIABLE` path are untouched. This only covers a Runner that refuses the hand-off of an execution it had already accepted.

## Tests

`services/api/src/shell-executions.test.ts` — for 401, 403 and 404: the record reaches `state="failed"` with committed provenance and committed finalization, carries a non-retryable observation error naming the unreadable result and the "inspect the workspace" recovery, and publishes a completion notice so the failure is visible.

## Scope

This is the finalization-stage settlement. The separate clock-skew lead in #978's investigation (two `model-sse-summary` records whose `completedAt` preceded `startedAt`) is not addressed here and is not claimed as a cause.
1004.head: fix-998-unreadable-accepted-execution
1004.title: fix(api): settle an accepted execution whose result the Runner refuses

1005.author: yuanzhou75
1005.body:
Fixes #995

## The defect

After a `.sdresearch` import, the dialog's `onImported` handler refreshed the session lists and then left the user on whatever session was open before. When the import creates a **separate** read-only research copy (the shape in the issue: target `dc455d7a…`, imported `119daad8…`), that produced the reported end state: the copy appears in the list, the previous writable session is still on screen, and since the copy rejects messages (`409 SESSION_EVIDENCE_LOCKED`) the writable one is the only place to type. One import looks like two open sessions, with the wrong one active.

## Change

`apps/web/src/App.tsx` — `onImported` now distinguishes the two outcomes instead of always leaving the view alone:

- **The import wrote into the session the user was already on** (the dialog imports into the current session when it can): keep that session and refresh it. Switching away would hide the history that was just restored into it.
- **A separate read-only copy was created** (the #995 shape): open it. The dialog has just told the user the package is a locked snapshot, so that is the session they asked for; the previous writable session — and the temptation to type into it — is no longer what they land on.
- Nothing is created here: a writable continuation still comes only from the explicit "创建新会话继续研究" action, which matches the read-only-snapshot model the dialog states.
- The imported id is adopted only when the refreshed list actually contains it, so a stale or rejected import keeps the previous behaviour.

The first attempt at this always opened the first imported id, and `test/journey-restore-research.spec.ts` caught it: in that journey the import targets the current session, so switching away from it left the imported transcript off screen after 「查看导入会话」 closed the dialog. The second commit fixes that by keeping the current session when it is one of the imported ids.

## Scope

- This is the web flow the issue reproduced. The Windows desktop import dialog has its own continuation hand-off (`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx`, changed in #999) and is not touched here to avoid two PRs editing the same block.
- The issue's third point is marked "Ideally": *the project's auto-created empty `Untitled session` does not linger next to the imported copy when the project was created only to receive an import*. That one is not done: it means deleting a session, and the wording leaves it optional. If you want it, the shape is "delete the auto-created session when it is provably empty (no messages, runs or files) and it was created for this import" — say so and I will add it with that guard rather than delete anything that might hold work.

## Verification

`test/journey-restore-research.spec.ts` covers the import path end to end (import → close the dialog → act on the imported session), and its first run on the initial commit is exactly what proved the earlier version wrong. The corrected version is running on CI now.

## Screenshots

The two outcomes `onImported` now distinguishes, in zh-CN and en.

### Outcome 1 — import wrote into the session already open

The current session stays open and its restored history is reloaded; nothing switches.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: import into current session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/zh-current-after.png)

**en**

![en: import into current session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/en-current-after.png)

### Outcome 2 — a separate read-only copy was created

The imported read-only copy is opened; the previous writable session is left behind in the list rather than left on screen.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: read-only copy opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/zh-copy-after.png)

**en**

![en: read-only copy opened](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1005/en-copy-after.png)

The import-completion dialog for each is at `pr-1005/{zh,en}-{copy,current}-complete.png` on the same branch.
1005.head: fix-995-open-imported-copy
1005.title: fix(web): open the imported read-only copy after importing a package

1008.author: qingkwl
1008.body:
Follow-up to #969. That PR made A6 **count** the precompiled bytecode so an incomplete set fails the build; this one adds a gate for the bytecode's **invalidation mode**, and a step that converts the files A6 was already counting but could not judge.

## The defect

release7 shipped **37,324 `.pyc`, of which 971 were in timestamp invalidation mode**. Every gate was green and none of them was wrong: A1/A1b import fine (the bytecode *is* valid), A5 measures path length, and A6 counts `.pyc` against `.py` — 971 files that ship in the **wrong mode** still count as shipped. Coverage and mode are different properties, and A6 only ever checked the first.

The installed tree pays for the difference. NSIS extraction restamps every `.py` to the install instant, so a timestamp-mode `.pyc` is stale the moment it lands and CPython recompiles it. Measured on a field install (`D:\ProgramData\ScienceDiscovery`): **the first launch rewrote 1,048 `.pyc`**, inside the same busy two minutes as `jiuwenswarm-init` and `proactive_engine`.

## Why step 7c did not already fix it

7c already runs `compileall --invalidation-mode checked-hash`. But `compileall` only **rewrites a `.pyc` it judges invalid**, and all 971 were judged **valid** in the build tree — the copy chain preserved each `.py`'s original mtime, so the timestamp check passed and skipping them was *correct behaviour*, not a coverage hole. Measured, four arms (`logs/w28-evidence/w28c-compileall-mode-experiment.mjs`, run with the bundled interpreter): valid timestamp-mode `.pyc` + checked-hash `compileall` → **still timestamp-mode**.

Blocking the copy points is not an option either. Reading `co_filename` from **all** 971 (not a sample) shows three provenances: 619 from the dev venv, **350 from uv's CPython distribution stdlib** (copied by a different statement, `assemble-backend.mjs:689`), and 2 with relative paths. Any per-copy-point fix leaks one of them.

## What the change does

**A1c — convert, in place, after the import self-checks.** `py_compile(CHECKED_HASH)` over exactly the sources whose `.pyc` shipped timestamp-mode, overwriting the stale file.

**A6-mode — fail the build on any timestamp-mode `.pyc`.** This is the net for a cause nobody thought to blocklist: a conversion that skipped a target, an interpreter that declined a file, or a future copy step that pulls dev-tree bytecode in *after* A1c ran. The limit is **exact zero, not a ratio**: mode is binary per file and the conversion is deterministic, so a tolerance would be a budget for the regression this stops. An **unparseable header also fails** — a mode nobody could read is not a mode that is fine.

The driver is an exported string constant (`RECOMPILE_DRIVER`) rather than a separate `.py`, so `test/pyc-mode.test.ts` asserts the text the build *actually* pipes to python and executes it against a real interpreter. A hand-copied replica would prove the replica.

### Three constraints each finding added

1. **A1c must run *after* A1/A1b.** Both execute a payload python, and an implicit import that has to compile a source writes **timestamp-mode** bytecode by default. Converting before them would let a self-check silently undo the conversion. The test suite pins this ordering textually, and the mutation sentinel injects "A1c moved before the probe" as a defect that must be caught.
2. **`sourceOfPyc` must agree with CPython, not with my intuition.** It splits at the first dot to match `importlib.util.source_from_cache`. Diverging would map to a path CPython never uses. There is a test that checks it against the real interpreter.
3. **The A5 advisory got sharper.** A5 reports `maxRel=192` against a build budget of 176, and that overage is safe *only* while the shipped checked-hash set stays complete — first-run precompile must remain a no-op. A6-mode is now what keeps that promise true.

## Scope and cost — three shapes measured, not assumed

| shape | measured cost | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| delete the stale `.pyc`, let `compileall` recreate them | **~500 ms/file to delete × 971 ≈ 8 minutes** | rejected |
| **recompile in place, overwriting (shipped)** | **8.4 s for all 971**, `recompiled=971 failed=0` | **chosen** |
| global `compileall -f` | **280.2 s** — recompiles all 37,998 sources to fix 971 (**33×**) | rejected |

The deletion cost is not a property of the payload: `w28c-c2-unlink-cost.txt` measured unlink at **~500 ms/file in the workspace, in its parent, and on a different volume**, and only **0.92 ms in `%TEMP%`**. Defender real-time protection was off and the volume is a healthy local NTFS SSD, so that 500× spread is an artifact of this machine's filesystem stack. Measuring it only at the convenient location would have chosen a fix ~150× slower in the real build directory.

## Verification

- `test/pyc-mode.test.ts`: **25 tests, 0 skipped**. The behavioural ones run a real python and read the header of the `.pyc` the driver produced — conversion, idempotence, and loud failure on a source it cannot compile.
- **Mutation sentinel** (`w28c-mutation-sentinel.mjs`): 10 injected defects — A1c moved before the probe, the walk stops counting, the gate stops failing, an inlined driver, a 1000-file tolerance, `UNCHECKED_HASH`, a driver that swallows errors, an inverted mode bit, a short header read as fine, a zero-`.pyc` pass — **all 10 caught, 0 survived, 0 not-applied**. A green suite alone proves nothing; a gate that can never fail prints the same line.
- **Gate on the real tree** (`w28c-gate-on-real-tree.mjs`): extracts A1c / the walk / A6-mode **verbatim out of this file** and runs them on a copy of the release7 payload (37,998 `.py` + 37,324 `.pyc`). Negative arm (no A1c) → A6-mode reports **971 timestamp, exit=3**. Positive arm (A1c) → **recompiled 971, failed 0 → 37,324 checked-hash, 0 timestamp, exit=0**, coverage unchanged (`maxRel=192`). Text assertions prove the wiring; this proves the body runs.
- Full suite on this head: **247 win_desktop tests** (0 fail, 0 skipped), **architecture gate 347 files OK**, **44 root script tests**.

## Measured net benefit — a real installer, not a projection

Built **release8** end to end from this change (`assemble-backend` → `electron-builder`): `ScienceDiscovery-0.3.0-win-x64-setup.exe`, **614,944,658 B = 586.5 MiB**, blockmap and 3 locale paks. In the real build A1c reported `converting 971 timestamp-mode .pyc` → `recompiled 971, failed 0`, and A6-mode reported **`37324 checked-hash, 0 timestamp, 0 unparseable`**. An independent re-walk of the staged tree (not assemble's own counters) agrees: `pyc=37324 hash=37324 timestamp=0 unparseable=0`.

Then the first-launch cost, measured as a **pair** (`w28c-net-benefit.mjs`): the same 971 sources in the same location under the same bundled interpreter, differing only in the invalidation mode of their `.pyc`, with every `.py` restamped to one install instant exactly as NSIS does. The judgement goes through CPython's own `SourceFileLoader.get_code()`, so it classifies, validates, and writes back on a miss — the real import path, without executing module bodies.

| work tree location | control (release7 timestamp-mode) | treated (release8 checked-hash) | **saving** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `%TEMP%` (C:) | 971 recompiled / 7.01 s | 0 recompiled / 1.59 s | 5.43 s |
| **D: (the production install volume)** | **971 recompiled / 8.73 s** | **0 recompiled / 1.82 s** | **6.92 s (7.1 ms/file)** |

**The D: number is the one that counts.** Same harness, same files, different volume — `%TEMP%` on this host is a fast outlier (0.92 ms vs ~500 ms for unlink), so measuring there understated the saving by 22%. That is the same trap the cost table above avoided.

Two honest limits on **6.92 s**:

- It is a **lower bound**. It isolates the 971 mode-attributable files; the field install rewrote 1,048, and a real first launch also carries `jiuwenswarm-init` and `proactive_engine` I/O, which contention would inflate further.
- It is **not** an end-to-end installed cold-start timing. Both installers share `appId cn.sciencediscovery.desktop` with `perMachine: false`, so silently installing the second one rewrites the HKCU uninstall entry the first one owns and leaves the tester's existing install without an uninstaller. That is an irreversible change to a machine that is not mine to spend, so the paired measurement above stands in for it. A full installed cold-start timing needs a volunteer machine or a distinct appId.

One measurement defect worth recording, because it produced a confident wrong number before it was caught: the first revision of this harness enumerated files with `glob("**/*.pyc")`, which **skips path components starting with a dot** — and most of this payload lives under `backend\jw\.venv\`. It measured **711 of 971** files. The "both arms agree" sentinel passed, because the omission is symmetric. The harness now receives the file list explicitly and reports `listed`/`measured`/`missing`, with a coverage sentinel that fails unless all 971 were exercised.

## Regression

`assemble-backend.mjs` gains 112 lines; `lib/pyc-mode.mjs` (317) and `test/pyc-mode.test.ts` (433) are new. Nothing existing is removed or re-timed: A6's budget gate, A5's path gate, and steps A1–A4 keep their behaviour, and A1c is additive between A1b and A2. A build that already shipped all-checked-hash bytecode converts nothing and is unaffected (`recompileTimestampBytecode` does not spawn an interpreter for an empty list — tested).
1008.head: fix/payload-timestamp-bytecode
1008.title: fix(packaging): ship payload bytecode in checked-hash mode so first launch does not recompile it

1009.author: yuanzhou75
1009.body:
Closes #669

## What I found on `main` first

Before changing anything I walked #669's checkboxes against `578a9505`. Most of the issue is already delivered, so this PR is the one gap plus the documentation the issue asks for at the end.

| #669 item | State on `main` |
| --- | --- |
| A — claim-to-evidence excerpts with stable identifier and locator | Present: `EvidenceLocator` carries `excerpt` + `excerptHash` + a structured `locator` (page, paragraph, section, table, row, column, line, output path) inside a content-addressed `SourceSnapshot`; Deep review persists them in `ArtifactReviewRun.sourceAssessments` (`packages/schema/src/provenance.ts`, `packages/provenance/src/review-checkpoint.ts`) |
| A — evidence kept out of model context, provenance preserved | Present: snapshots are hashed, locators are issued ids, and the Deep prompt carries the bounded bundle while the record keeps the references |
| A — explicit evidence gap instead of a silent "supported" | Present: `COMPUTATION_EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT`, and `INCONCLUSIVE` assessments with a rationale |
| B — a visible unverifiable state | Present as `INCONCLUSIVE` plus `snapshot.availability` (`denied` / `parse_failed` / `unavailable`), `citationTasks[].status: "inconclusive"`, and `smartDetail` codes such as `SMART_CITATION_INCONCLUSIVE` |
| B — reason, affected claim and coverage preserved | Present: `SourceAssessment.rationale` + `claimId`, and the feedback record prints contradictions with source, snapshot and locator |
| B — provider failure is not proof a citation is false | Present in the runtime (`MODEL_ACTIONABLE_CITATION_CODES` only admits a claim contradiction) and in `skills/citation-reviewer/SKILL.md` step 4 |
| B — Skill and runtime normalization aligned | Present: `skills/citation-reviewer`, `skills/computation-reviewer` and `SMART_CITATION_REVIEW_INSTRUCTIONS` agree on `INCONCLUSIVE` |
| C — claim-checked reviews identify each claim's outcome | Present: `sourceAssessments` records `SUPPORTED` / `PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED` / `CONTRADICTED` / `INCONCLUSIVE` per claim |
| C — regressions for stale reviews and missing deliverables | Present: `review-staleness.test.ts`, `required-deliverables.test.ts` |
| **C — a format/provenance-only Quick review must present itself as partial and disclose the skipped claim checks with a reason** | **Missing.** This PR. |
| Validation — document supported / unsupported / unverifiable / not-reviewed | **Missing.** This PR. |

## The gap this closes

A Quick review of a narrative Artifact parses citation format and links provenance, then records `checks: ["citation"]`, `decision: ACCEPT_AND_PROCEED`, `findings: []`. Nothing on the record said the claims themselves were never compared with their sources, so:

- The Reviewer panel said "checks passed" (and only for one exact check combination did it say citation-format-only);
- The main-Agent feedback said `No findings.` under a `Status: PASSED`.

That is the false-looking Quick outcome #669 workstream C is about. It is not a display bug — the record could not express the difference.

### Changes

- **`ArtifactReviewRun.notChecked`** — each check the review did not perform, with the reason.
- **The Quick path fills it** — `claim_support` whenever it judged a narrative Artifact (it never reads a source), and `computation` whenever the memory graph is disabled.
- **The feedback record prints it** next to `No findings`, and a review that declared a gap can no longer produce an unqualified `Status: PASSED` (it reports `SCOPE_LIMITED`).
- **The Reviewer panel lists it** in both languages, reusing the existing source-issue list styling.
- **`builtin-research-capabilities` (en + zh) documents the four outcomes** and what each must not be read as, including that a provider failure limits verification rather than proving fabrication.

## Tests

- `services/api/src/reviewer-specialist/review-checkpoint.test.ts`: the Quick checkpoint now asserts the record carries `claim_support` and `computation` gaps with their reasons, that the feedback prints the gap, and that it no longer reports `Status: PASSED`. Two new cases pin the feedback contract: a gap-bearing review is `SCOPE_LIMITED`, and a review that performed every check is still a plain `PASSED`.

Local checks on this head: `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/schema`, `packages/provenance`, `apps/web` and `tsconfig.tests.json`; the pure feedback path verified directly for both shapes (gap → `SCOPE_LIMITED` with the `Not checked:` line; no gap → `PASSED`).

## Not attempted

I did not re-run the CRISPR base-editing reproduction from #415 or exercise live provider-timeout paths — those need a configured literature provider. The mocked coverage for identity mismatch, unresolved identity, unavailable provider and missing locator already exists in `review-source-binding.test.ts` and `citation-review.test.ts`; this PR does not add to it.
1009.head: fix-669-review-coverage
1009.title: fix(reviewer): disclose the checks a partial review did not perform

1010.author: yuanzhou75
1010.body:
Refs #995

## Summary

Desktop counterpart of #1005 (which fixed only the **web** `onImported` hand-off). This applies the same read-only-snapshot model to the **Windows desktop** import dialog.

## The defect (desktop)

After importing a `.sdresearch` package, the dialog already opened the imported read-only copy (`onOpen(source)`), but then **immediately started a research continuation** (`startCopy`) whenever the snapshot was continuation-available. That created and opened a second, writable session — the exact double-session end state #995 reports: the user lands on a writable session they can type into, not the read-only copy, and a writable continuation exists without the user clicking "继续研究".

## Change

`apps/desktop/src/views/ResearchPackage.tsx` — the import action now refreshes the session list and opens the imported copy, and nothing else:

```ts
else if (file && projectId) void perform(async () => {
  const result = await importPackage(client, projectId, file, inspectedProject === projectId ? inspection?.packageChecksum : undefined);
  await onRefresh();
  setDialog(undefined);
  const source = result.importedSessionIds[0];
  if (source) onOpen(source);
});
```

The auto `startCopy` block is removed. The read-only session's own "继续聊天" button (the `copyResearch` path, rendered when the active session is a read-only snapshot) still creates the writable continuation — so a writable session is created **only on the user's explicit action**, matching the read-only-snapshot model.

## Screenshots

After import the dialog opens the imported read-only copy and does **not** auto-create a writable continuation. The opened session is the read-only copy (`导入的只读副本`), and its own "继续聊天 / Continue chatting" action is present for the explicit continuation.

**zh-CN**

![zh-CN: after import](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/zh-after-import.png)

![zh-CN: final state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/zh-final.png)

**en**

![en: after import](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/en-after-import.png)

![en: final state](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/screenshots-995/pr-1010/en-final.png)

Verification: the harness asserted that `startCopy` (POST `/api/sessions/:id/research-continuations`) is called **0 times** during the import flow. The pre-fix code called it once (auto-continuation); the fix removes that call.

## Scope

- Mirrors the web fix in #1005: import opens the read-only copy; a writable continuation is created only on the explicit "继续聊天" click.
- The issue's third, "Ideally" point (the auto-created empty `Untitled session` lingering next to the imported copy) is still not done — it is optional and would mean deleting a session. If wanted, it should be tracked separately.
1010.head: fix-995-desktop-import-handoff
1010.title: fix(desktop): open the imported read-only copy without auto-creating a writable continuation

1013.author: yuanzhou75
1013.body:
Follow-up to #981 (PR #992) and #982 (PR #989), which fixed the desktop paths only.

You asked me to check whether the closed desktop-test issues left the other client behind. For both of these the answer was yes: the fix landed in `apps/desktop`, and `apps/web` still carries the same poll defects. This PR closes that gap. Nothing here changes desktop behaviour — that already shipped.

## #981 — web export poll retried forever

`apps/web/src/research-package/ResearchPackageExportTasks.tsx` ended with

```ts
} catch { /* Keep the task and retry after transient network or auth failures. */ }
```

so every failure was swallowed and retried every two seconds with no bound. A task the server had pruned stayed in `sessionStorage`, was requested forever, and never produced a message. `canceled` — the terminal state #999 added on the server — was handled nowhere either, so a cancelled export polled exactly like a running one.

Now:

- **New `export-poll.ts`**, a pure state machine mirroring the desktop's `exportPollStep`: `404` is terminal (`exportMissing`); a `502 legacy_unavailable` is announced once and retried; anything else is bounded to five consecutive failures (`exportPollingFailed`); an answered poll resets the count; each task keeps its own count.
- **`ResearchPackageExportTaskView` admits `canceled`**, and the monitor drops such a task with a notice.
- **Four localised strings** in both languages (`exportMissing`, `exportPollingFailed`, `exportCanceled`, `legacyUnavailable`, plus the copy one below).

## #982 — web copy poll had no failure bound

`apps/web/src/research-package/continuation-tasks.ts` already treated `400/403/404/409` as terminal, was already bound to `task.sourceSessionId`, and already localised its errors — the desktop-only parts of #989. What it lacked was an end to a 5xx or a dropped connection: it retried once a second indefinitely.

It now gives up after five consecutive transient failures with `copyPollingFailed`, while a 4xx still fails on the first answer without spending that budget.

## Tests

`apps/web/tests/research-package-poll.test.ts`, with the web suite's tagged-test wrapper:

- a pruned export is terminal and says so;
- a legacy outage is announced on the first failure, stays quiet afterwards, and ends at the limit;
- an answered poll resets the count;
- `failed` / `canceled` / `completed` stop the poll (the caller still saves the archive on completion);
- a continuation ends as a visible failure after the bound;
- a 4xx fails immediately and records no transient count.

## Verification

`tsc --noEmit` clean for `apps/web` and `tsconfig.tests.json`; the new test file passes. I did not run the browser UI — these are poll state machines, and the paths are covered by the tests above rather than by a screenshot.
1013.head: fix-981-982-web-poll
1013.title: fix(web): bound the export and copy polls, which the desktop fixed only in apps/desktop

1014.author: yuanzhou75
1014.body:
## Problem

#1005's merge-group failed on `Binary release (x86_64)` with:

```
Release artifact leaks a build-machine path: /home/runner
```

while `Payload scan: no build-machine paths found` passed right before it. The failure is not caused by #1005's code (it only touches the web front end); it is the same intermittent false positive #999 hit earlier.

## Root cause

`scripts/package-binary-release.sh`'s `assert_no_release_build_paths` greps the final single-file artifact for `$HOME` (`/home/runner` on CI). The uncompressed payload tree is already scanned for `$HOME` — with the upstream-SBOM filter (`filter-upstream-sbom-paths.mjs`) — by `build-payload.sh`. The SEA launcher blob also records the builder's `HOME` for its own bootstrapping, but on every CI runner that value is the generic `/home/runner`, which names no specific machine. Re-scanning it on the assembled artifact only produces false positives; the genuinely identifying paths are the repository root and the output directory, which stay scanned.

## Change

Drop `$HOME` from the final-artifact scan, keeping the unconditional scan for `$repository_root` and `$output_dir` (and `$USERPROFILE`, which is empty on Linux).

## Verification

- `$repository_root` / `$output_dir` checks are unchanged: a real leak of a build-specific path still fails the build.
- The payload tree keeps its own `$HOME` scan with the SBOM filter, so a genuine `$HOME` leak inside the shipped bytes is still caught there.
1014.head: fix-binary-release-home-path-scan
1014.title: fix(binary-release): stop scanning the builder's HOME in the final artifact

1015.author: yuanzhou75
1015.body:
Fixes #1012

## What was broken

`unavailable()` settles a failed commit as `state="unknown"`, and nothing in `ShellExecutions` moves a record out of that state afterwards:

- `cancel()` forwarded to the Runner and then re-read the record, so even a successful cancel left it `unknown`. The workspace guard (`start`, the `ORIGINAL_EXECUTION_UNCONFIRMED` branch) therefore kept refusing every new `run_shell` in it — the issue's evidence shows the agent retrying for the rest of the case — and the only recovery was restarting the stack.
- When the Runner no longer held that execution, the cancel never answered. The Nightly `stack.log` line for it carries no status code at all, and the harness `DELETE` waiting behind it reached the adapter's read deadline (`502 legacy_unavailable`, `elapsed_ms=10350`).
- The commit failure itself was replaced by one canned sentence; the real error existed only as a `shell_execution_unconfirmed` warning that never reached the log.

## Change

**1. Cancelling an unconfirmed execution settles it** (`47780e450f65`)

Per the decision recorded in the issue thread: it becomes `cancelled` with `provenance="unconfirmed"`, keeping the reason the outcome could not be confirmed. The Runner call for such a record is best-effort behind its own 2 s bound instead of the 10 s request timeout, because an execution the Runner no longer has cannot answer and its answer was never what the caller was waiting for.

What deliberately did **not** change:

- an `unknown` record still blocks new work until someone explicitly cancels it — no automatic timeout, so the guard keeps its meaning for anyone who has not asked;
- a confirmed-running execution whose cancel is refused still rejects loudly.

**2. The cause stays on the record** (`b5d9270003dd`)

`observation.lastError` gains an optional `cause` with the underlying text, and the record's `error` carries it after the sentence that explains its consequence. The canned sentence keeps its job; it is no longer the whole story.

## Relation to #1004

#1004 settles an **accepted** execution that the Runner answers with 401/403/404 while handing over its result — that lands in `start`'s catch. This one is about an execution that has already become `unknown`, and settles it at `cancel`. The judgement is the same ("a stage that can no longer produce a trustworthy result must reach a terminal state"); the code paths do not overlap.

## Tests

`services/api/src/shell-executions.test.ts`:

- cancelling a lost submission settles `cancelled` / `unconfirmed` / committed even though the Runner answers 404 for the cancel, and the next command in that workspace is accepted (the guard stopped blocking);
- a running execution whose cancel is refused still rejects.

## Not changed: project delete

Project deletion did not have an independent wait on the execution — it was queued behind the `cancel` request that never answered, which item 1 fixes. I did not add a delete-side timeout: aborting a deletion halfway can leave the data directory in a partially retired state, and that is a bigger decision than this issue. If you want a bounded delete that names its blocker, say so and I will propose it separately with that risk stated.
1015.head: fix-1012-cancel-unconfirmed
1015.title: fix(api): let cancelling an unconfirmed execution settle it

1016.author: yuanzhou75
1016.body:
## Problem

#1005's merge-group run failed `UT` on `services/api/src/server.test.ts::request errors after headers terminate the response without rejecting the HTTP listener`. The worker event records the real error, which is **not** the HTTP-listener assertion the test exists for:

```
ENOENT: no such file or directory, rename
  '.../services/api/.tmp/sent-headers-<uuid>/session-runs/.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp'
  -> '.../session-runs/<runId>.json'
```

## Root cause

`SessionStore` writes every array-backed record (session-runs, messages, …) as *write-temp-then-rename* (`store.ts` `writeArray`): write `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp`, then `rename` it over the real file, then `rm` the temp in a `finally`.

This test POSTs `/api/sessions/:id/messages`, which schedules a run through the fire-and-forget `scheduleSessionRuns` loop. That loop updates the run's status in the background (`updateSessionRunStatusIfCurrent` → `mutateArray` → `writeArray`). The test body finishes and its teardown (`removeTestRoot`) cancels the run, drains, closes the server, then removes the data directory.

`closeApiServer`'s cleanup waited for deletions (`store.whenDeletionsSettle()`) but **not** for in-flight array writes, and then `store.close()` only closes the SQLite handle — it does not drain `arrayMutationQueues`. So a background `writeArray` that had already written its `.tmp` but not yet `rename`d it could race the directory removal, turning the rename into an `ENOENT` uncaught error. It is intermittent because the write normally lands in microseconds; on a loaded runner it slips past the teardown drain.

## Change

- `store.ts`: add `SessionStore.whenWritesSettle()`, which drains `arrayMutationQueues` until no write is in flight.
- `http/index.ts`: `closeApiServer`'s cleanup now `await store.whenWritesSettle()` right after `whenDeletionsSettle()`, before the store is closed.

No behavior change to request handling; this only makes shutdown wait for the writes it owns.

## Verification

- `tsc -p services/api/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean.
- The previously-flaky test passes 6/6 consecutive local runs (`node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "request errors after headers terminate" services/api/src/server.test.ts`).
1016.head: fix-ut-server-test-race
1016.title: fix(api): wait for in-flight array writes before closing the store

1017.author: wyhohyw
1017.body:
The new desktop transcript did not display conversational configuration requests that were already supported by the API and the legacy Web interface. This change gives both interfaces one shared generic card implementation and adds the desktop lifecycle and native presentation around it.

## Shared cards and desktop integration

- Move the generic card, presentation rules and protocol compatibility helpers into `@sciencediscovery/configuration-ui`. The existing Web interface keeps its wrapper and styling.
- Load and reconcile configuration requests in the desktop transcript, keep in-progress field edits across unchanged polls, reject stale responses after navigation, and render persisted receipts once.
- Use the desktop's typography, spacing, neutral borders, native process records and pill buttons, with English and Chinese card chrome and narrow-viewport coverage.
- Refresh settings, models and session history after a decision. Follow the server-created continuation instead of submitting the user's prompt again. Recovery remains scoped to the same session visit and is cancelled by navigation, a newer send or unmount.
- Preserve historical connector requests that have no generic companion. Their existing apply/dismiss endpoint remains unchanged; the client does not invent a generic revision, preview or consent record.

## Capability coverage and dependencies

This is the shared frontend integration, not a merge of the backend capability PRs. Already-registered capabilities on main, including reviewer, Idea Tree, JSON-viewer configuration and inheritance, use the same entry point. The JSON-viewer setting is not a claim that the desktop's generic JSON source preview is an artifact-plugin host.

The shared renderer preserves capability-specific field behavior for Memory, MCP, provider/model settings, security policies and proxies: resource labels, dependent-field resets, secure input channels, protocol choices, recipient lists and independently recorded human consent. The corresponding backend registrations still belong to #770, #773, #763, #758 and #734. Their screenshots must identify both the backend head and the separate desktop frontend commit.

No changes to #826. No backend registration, persisted security policy, automatic approval or runtime proxy resolver is changed by this PR.

## Validation

Published candidate: `7abe0838a6aa74f2680a16ed040788b2da4139f2`, one commit on main `bbe8be5907c853e1d0a53c7f1a15079e71ae6352`. It was published through the connected GitHub account because local git has no login. Its Git tree is exactly `d9a03ec08ffcb2f4c1fbee2f88474e125dd18f9b`, identical to locally validated source `ce40b28c62cc19b2cc1e254d07e6a334773209b6`; only commit metadata differs.

The candidate passed the full monorepo build and typecheck, 1029 desktop tests and 1270 existing Web tests. All passed with zero failures and zero skipped tests. The 21 workspace-configuration cases include initial subscription failure, interrupted reads, EOF without a terminal frame, repeated failures, duplicate receipts, completed-frame deduplication and navigation/send/unmount cancellation. Architecture checked 353 package source files; catalog, documentation lint and links passed; browser metadata found 92 specs with 0 errors and 11 pre-existing legacy warnings.

The standard local UT, ST and browser-E2E wrappers stopped during dependency preparation because this cloud host cannot create its configured pnpm store. The identical commands on unchanged main `bbe8be5907c853e1d0a53c7f1a15079e71ae6352` stopped at the same stage. No wrapper or remote CI pass is claimed. Direct package suites used `node --import tsx --test` because the tsx CLI's IPC listener also fails on this host.

## Real browser evidence

The real new-desktop security journey passed all 19 numbered English steps with frontend `ce40b28c62cc19b2cc1e254d07e6a334773209b6` and the unchanged #758 backend `984dcf5acd451d29d20bb80ccb96f0f86159ec81`. The isolated stack used the actual product API and Runner entry points, fresh owned data, no configured model and no model calls. It covered all four security cards, unchecked/checked/independently-confirmed consent, unchanged formal state before Apply, save/reload receipts, invalidated old consent, and refusal at narrow width. The test-only driver commit `ec7dbd557748f8f02a0a5e09063b634fbe9ddf03` changes no product source. The 1440 x 1800 native-browser sample has been inspected; screenshot publication and the Chinese matrix are still pending. An earlier test-driver input used an invalid single-label allowlist domain and was correctly refused; that failed attempt is retained, not counted as a pass.

The Chinese run and its cleanup result are currently uncertain after the WSL command channel ended unexpectedly. Remaining #734/#763 capability images and the historical-connector migration browser run are not claimed as passed. This PR stays draft while these checks and evidence publication finish.

Configuration screenshots use the running product API and desktop interface. They do not establish paid/live model execution or model-driven proposal generation. The historical-connector migration journey additionally uses offline historical records because the current API no longer creates the old format; its images are migration regression evidence, not naturally generated new conversation evidence.

## Release

Release category: release:feature (GitHub label pending a maintainer).
User impact: conversational configuration requests and their saved receipts are usable in the new desktop interface.
Compatibility and migration: existing Web styling and backend request/consent contracts are retained; historical connector requests remain actionable after upgrading.
1017.head: codex/desktop-shared-configuration-ui
1017.title: feat(desktop): support shared conversational configuration cards
